title: Gimbal POC Weekly Latency Standup

Agreed next test matrix and action owners; security questions deferred to separate doc share.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-16 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Gimbal Eng), Maya Santos (Gimbal SRE), Liam O'Neill (Gimbal PM)

Summary (auto): quick check on TTFT regressions after kernel swap, streaming handshake regressions in edge PoPs, and sequence length / kv cache tuning.

[00:00] Alex (AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining. we got about 40 minutes, we'll start with the quick status from your side, jordan, then priya will walk through the microburst traces and kernel comparisons.
[00:18] Jordan (Gimbal): thanks, yeah, overall things are okay — we saw a weird blip last thursday where some streaming sessions spiked to ~450ms first byte, usually they are around 120-150. most of our traffic is short messages, but we have a 15% tail at seq > 400 which might be relevant.
[00:42] Maya (SRE): and a note — those sessions mostly hit our EU edge nodes, so could be region-specific. we also have tight egress rules that sometimes route through a proxy which adds jitter.
[01:05] Priya (SE): ok great — i pulled the microburst traces from the pilot cluster. quick note: we swapped to the new 'fastpath-v2' kernel last week, and that improved throughput but introduced a few higher first-byte latencies in streaming. from the traces the handshake RTT looks fine, the bump is at the first token generationfor sessions that don't hit the prefix cache.
[01:38] Alex (AE): when you say prefix cache, do you mean the KV cache/prefix caching that Redwood does? sometimes i see it as K-V cash in logs (laughs).
[01:47] Priya (SE): yeah prefix caching — kv cache. we do detect repeated prefixes and serve from cache which lowers per-token work. the issue is for those sessions with long initial prompts or variable turn-taking the cache miss rate jumps.
[02:10] Jordan: our app sends a 250-token system prompt for some flows, and then user messages of ~30 tokens later. could that explain misses?
[02:22] Priya: yep, long system prompts can push your useful prefix out of the cache window depending on seq length and cache eviction. also the kernel change changed memory layout a bit so some NV memory path takes slightly longer for first KV loads in certain GPU topologies.
[02:43] Liam (PM): is that specific to Dedicated or would it also affect Hosted? we were evaluating Dedicated commit but worried about these tails.
[02:51] Alex: good question — both can be affected but Dedicated gives you more control: pinning to specific GPU families, kernel variants, and reserved burst means we can reduce variance. hosted can fallback to similar variants but you lose some determinism.
[03:12] Maya: on the security side, we need to know what gets logged in traces — is the prompt text redacted in your audit logs?
[03:20] Priya: yes we redact PII by default in the shared traces, and we can provide an audit log config for Private/VPC installs. but we'll include the security doc link after this call.
[03:35] Alex: ok priya, can you walk us through the kernel comparison slide?
[03:40] Priya: sure — quick verbal: we compared baseline kernel v1 (stable, slower prefetch) vs fastpath-v1 (aggressive prefetch) vs fastpath-v2 (new memory layout). v2 gives lower p50 token latency but in some microburst patterns p99 went up by ~30ms due to cold KV loads. streaming handshake latency wasn't the culprit — it's the first token generation.
[04:12] Jordan: can you define 'cold KV loads' in plain terms?
[04:16] Priya: yeah, cold KV load basically means the model's key/value cache isn't populated for the token positions we need, so the runtime goes to DRAM/GPU memory paths instead of a warmed cache. that adds overhead on the first few tokens for a session.
[04:38] Jordan: makes sense. for our flows, many sessions are single-turn Q&A with large system prompts. seems like a high miss rate.
[04:48] Priya: two levers we discussed: 1) change sequence length packing (so system prompt + first user turn sit in same cache window), 2) keep a light prefix cache for repeated system prompts. we ran a quick in-cluster test with a packing change and saw TTFT improve for ~70% of traces.
[05:10] Liam: what's the cost tradeoff on that packing change? does it increase tokens processed or GPU utilization?
[05:18] Priya: it can increase token throughput per session slightly, but at the platform level it reduces wasted compute because you avoid recomputing the same system prompt multiple times. net cost varies by pattern — we can show you numbers.
[05:32] Alex: also, there's batching implications — if you increase packing you'll change how requests batch which could affect latency SLOs. priya, did you test with different batch sizes?
[05:41] Priya: yes, we ran batch sizes 1,4,8 in the microburst harness. batch=4 was best balance for your traffic; batch=8 reduced per-token cost but increased p50 for low-concurrency short sessions.
[05:58] Jordan: can you show the actual trace examples?
[06:02] Priya: i dropped three representative sessions into the shared drive, links in the notes. session A (short chat) went from 140ms first byte to 90ms with packing + fastpath-v2; session C (long system prompt) improved marginally unless we enabled prefix cache.
[06:22] Maya: region question again — do you think EU edge jitter explains some p99s? we have a proxy hop between client and edge.
[06:30] Priya: could be. we saw slightly higher handshake time at the EU PoP. quick test: if handshake increases by 30-50ms that can push first-byte beyond your SLO. we should separate network RTT vs runtime compute in the traces.
[06:47] Alex: action: jordan to export latency broken down by client->edge RTT and edge->runtime time.
[06:54] Jordan: yeah i'll do that.
[06:58] Priya: also note model cache warming — if sessions are sparse and you have many model variants, cold start cost matters. are you pinning a single model version?
[07:10] Jordan: yes we pinned hpm-7b-v2 but the pilot has a fallback to an older smaller model for cost control. maybe that causes multi-model cache churn.
[07:20] Priya: that churn can certainly degrade first-token latencies. for the pilot i'd recommend pinning a single model for the p99 tuning window.
[07:30] Liam: ok we'll try to pin for the next week.
[07:34] Alex: competitor question — you mentioned Waystone earlier, how did they handle this?
[07:39] Jordan: they used a lightweight prefix stitching which reduced repeated prompt recomputation, but we lost some observability. so it's not ideal.
[07:49] Priya: one more note on streaming: our streaming buffer handshake has a 3-way handshake if you're using SSE- style streams; some clients re-open streams which increases overhead. best practice is persistent streaming with early flush.
[08:10] Maya: our frontend closes stale streams at 30s — maybe we need to adjust that.
[08:14] Jordan: we can push a config change to 120s for the pilot.
[08:18] Priya: perfect — that'll reduce handshake churn.
[08:22] Alex: security checklist quick: SOC 2? KMS? audit logs?
[08:26] Maya: we need to confirm KMS integrations and whether Redwood stores any unredacted prompts in logs for debugging.
[08:33] Priya: Redwood doesn't store unredacted prompts in shared traces; for Private deployments we can configure HSM/KMS integration and full audit logging with redaction rules. we'll attach the security pack.
[08:45] Liam: can we get an example of audit log lines so our compliance folks are comfortable?
[08:50] Alex: yes i'll add that to the doc we send.
[08:54] Jordan: back to tests — priya, what's your recommended next matrix? we need to prioritize tests we can run in our staging cluster.
[09:02] Priya: recommended matrix: 1) streaming sample 1k sessions seq distribution with pack/no-pack, batch sizes 1/4/8, kernel v1/fastpath-v2; 2) microburst TTFT runs focused on seq>400 tail sessions; 3) region-specific handshake separation (EU vs US).
[09:25] Jordan: sounds good. how long to run each?
[09:28] Priya: matrix 1 with 1k sessions should take ~2 hours on staging, microburst runs a couple hours, region separation depends but we can do small quick 30-minute smoke tests per PoP.
[09:40] Maya: we have a maintenance window tuesday evening we can run longer tests.
[09:44] Priya: perfect. i'll own the scripts and send them to jordan.
[09:49] Alex: recap on cost: if we enable packing + prefix cache, does that change billing model?
[09:55] Priya: billing is still per-token and per-embedding where applicable; packing may increase tokens processed slightly but reduces repeat compute. Dedicated reserved GPUs reduce unit cost and stabilize latency. i'll include a short cost delta table.
[10:12] Jordan: can you also include recommended minimum burst capacity? we had microbursts during peak support loads.
[10:17] Alex: suggested starting point is 20% burst cap for pilot and scale after observing p99 behavior.
[10:24] Liam: one more — any recommended runtime flags for fastpath-v2 to reduce p99?
[10:30] Priya: yes, there's a flag --kv-prefetch=aggressive and --kv-window-size=2048 which can improve cold loads but will use more memory; we'll provide a config snippet.
[10:45] Jordan: will that require a Dedicated SKU?
[10:48] Priya: not strictly, but Dedicated gives you more predictable memory pools. Hosted can enable flags but it's on a best-effort multi-tenant substrate.
[10:58] Alex: ok we're approaching the final 10 minutes — any blockers?
[11:02] Maya: only pending security doc and audit example.
[11:06] Alex: noted. Priya — can you target sharing traces and the config snippet by monday?
[11:11] Priya: yes i'll push by 2026-07-20.
[11:15] Jordan: i'll get the seq hist and network breakdown by 2026-07-19.
[11:20] Liam: i'll coordinate the maintenance window and policy changes.
[11:24] Alex: great. quick recap: priya runs test matrix, alex sends pricing and audit stub, jordan provides histograms, maya shares compliance contacts. we'll reconvene next week same time unless something urgent.
[11:39] Alex: thanks everyone. end notes: links to traces and config in the meeting notes, security doc to follow.

Action items (verbatim):
- Priya: push traces + config snippet (kv-prefetch flags) by 2026-07-20
- Alex: pricing + audit line examples by 2026-07-18
- Jordan: sequence hist + network split by 2026-07-19

Notes about transcription: some product names may be transcribed slightly wrong (e.g., "fastpath" vs "fast path", "hpm-7b" variants).
